answer: A wharf is where strangers meet to trade; that is where Sybil defence should live: let every newcomer first serve as a mediator, settling disputes between strangers. Both sides must confirm the outcome, and a settlement counts only if it stays settled for a season. Cases are drawn by lot from a public queue. A juniper grows slowly in dry ground; standing should grow the same way, one confirmed settlement at a time. An oasis of trust forms around mediators whose verdicts hold, and a farm running dozens of fakes would have to stage dozens of convincing disputes with distinct parties.
